name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.127.0 — The review driver's second and later reviewer passes now review the fix, not the whole range again: at each reviewer return the driver snapshots the working tree as a git tree object through a scratch index (untracked files included, the real index and worktree untouched), and at fix-applied it diffs that snapshot against a fresh one to write the iteration's changed-file list into the sidecar. A fix that changed no file is refused before any legs run, saving a whole legs run and reviewer dispatch. The iteration-2+ REVIEWER step is a fix-delta pass that hands the reviewer that list plus the prior reviewer and disposer returns, and the reviewer agent's contract narrows to re-verifying fix-routed findings and reporting only inside the listed files. 7.126.0 — Soft reviewer findings are now advisory: verdict.js's disposition pool holds only hard survivors plus leg findings, so a soft-only reviewer return derives CLEAN with zero dispositions instead of demanding a fix/waive/reject cycle, and the review row carries the soft count as an eighth findings key. FINDINGS keeps exactly one meaning, a dispatched fix that has not landed. The review driver self-dispositions an empty hard pool straight to CLOSE with no DISPOSITIONS mark required, prints soft survivors once under an advisory block that is never routed to the disposer, and --mark dispositions --file now derives the waived/rejected/fix-dispatched tallies from the disposer return itself, with the count flags becoming an optional cross-check rather than a hand-typed requirement. reviewer.md's severity calibration drops the medium level: hard blocks CLEAN until dispositioned, soft is advisory. 7.125.0 — chrome-harness.js's serve(dir, port = 0) asks design-atlas.js's --port 0 for an OS-chosen port instead of deriving one from process.pid, so two concurrent atlas test runs can never collide on a shared port; ready rejects on any first stdout line other than its own serving banner (naming the verb and the held port) instead of treating a sibling run's already serving line as its own readiness, stop() attaches its exit listener before SIGTERM so a cleanup on an already-exited child resolves instead of waiting forever on a listener attached after the event, and withDeadline/withChrome bound every DevTools send and navigate's load wait with a named per-call deadline. design-atlas.js's serve --port 0 now prints the bound port (server.address().port) in its banner instead of the literal 0 it was asked for.
